Markdown: Cap ordered list mark at 999,999,999 (#19351 by @​tats-u)

CommonMark parsers only support ordered list item numbers up to 999,999,999.

With this change, Prettier now caps the ordered list item number at 999,999,999 to ensure that the output is correctly parsed as an ordered list by CommonMark parsers. Numbers larger than 999,999,999 are not parsed as list item numbers and are left unchanged in the output:

1234567890123456789012) text


<!-- Prettier 3.9.5 -->
999999998. text
999999999. text
999999999. text
999999999. text


1234567890123456789012) text

Markdown: Avoid corrupting empty link with title (#19487 by @​andersk)

Do not remove <> from an inline link or image with an empty URL and a title, as this removal would change its interpretation.

[link](https://github.com/prettier/prettier/blob/main/<> "title")

title: feat(018): optional Redis infra: typed baseline client + opt-in infra.config contract
body:
## What

Ship `apps/api/lib/redis.ts`, the single baseline seam that reads the fully
typed `REDIS_HOST` / `REDIS_USER` / `REDIS_PASSWORD` Redis connection triple
(parallel to the app's Postgres `SQL_HOST` / `SQL_USERNAME` / `SQL_PASSWORD`
contract). There is no `REDIS_URL`: one typed triple is the whole contract, so
nothing clashes.

New spec `018-optional-redis-infra` establishes the client and the contract.

## Why

Redis is being promoted from an inert, falsely-labelled marker to a real,
opt-in infrastructure resource across three repos (this baseline,
factory-encore spec 008, OAP spec 227). This PR is the baseline link: the
canonical typed client that produced apps use, landed here so the cron
scheduler's large-scale lock can reference it and lockstep can pin it.

## Design

- **Lazy + dormant.** `getRedis()` constructs the ioredis client on first use
  and memoizes it; an app that never sets `REDIS_HOST` opens no socket, and
  `isRedisConfigured()` lets an optional consumer branch (small vs large tier)
  without touching Redis. `encore check` and boot pass with Redis absent.
- **Opt-in, not baseline topology.** The `infra.config.json` `redis` block that
  declares the resource is composed by the factory `data-redis` module
  (factory-encore spec 008), not shipped in the lean baseline. Encore accepts
  such a block without a `CacheCluster` in code (verified against Encore
  v1.57.9).
- **Honest role.** Redis is not the rate-limit backend (that is Postgres,
  INV-6) and not a session store (sessions are stateless JWT, INV-3 / INV-7).
  Its first concrete consumer is the cron scheduler's large-scale distributed
  lock.

## Verification

- `apps/api/lib/redis.test.ts`: 6 unit tests (host/port parsing, configured
  detection). All pass.
- `encore check`: parse + type-check + boot pass (against a fresh local DB).
- `spec-spine compile` / `lint --fail-on-warn` / `index check`: clean.

## Companions

- factory-encore spec 008: composes the `redis` block and migrates the cron
  lock onto this typed client.
- OAP spec 227: surfaces Redis as an opt-in create-project resource and
  provisions it in dev via deployd `previewRedis`.

title: fix(016): keep the docs Pages workflow inert until an admin enables Pages
body:
## What

The produced-repo "Deploy docs to GitHub Pages" workflow (`deploy-docs.yml`, established by spec 016) hard-failed on a freshly produced repo. `actions/configure-pages` was called with no enablement guard, so on a repo where Pages has never been enabled it 404s ("Get Pages site failed") and the first push to `main` goes red.

That directly violates **spec 016 FR-04**, which requires the workflow to be **inert until a repo admin enables GitHub Pages** (§5 keeps enabling Pages an out-of-scope repo-admin action).

## Fix

Add a `preflight` job that queries `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pages` with the workflow's `github.token` and gates `build`/`deploy` on the result:

- **Pages disabled** → `enabled=false` → `build` and `deploy` skip via a job-level `if`, so the run concludes **green** (skipped jobs do not fail the run). Genuinely inert.
- **Pages enabled** (admin action) → `enabled=true` → the next qualifying run builds and publishes exactly as before.

Enablement is **not** auto-performed (no `configure-pages` `enablement: true`): that would contradict FR-04's admin-gated design and §5. The workflow never enables Pages itself.

## Spec + governance

- FR-04 refined to specify the inertness mechanism (previously asserted, now precise and matched by the code).
- Regenerated the 016 registry + index shards.
- Green locally: AC-2 pins lint (exit 0), `spec-spine lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0), `index check` (fresh), coupling gate (no drift). `.github/**` sits in the coupling bypass floor, so the workflow edit alone does not trip the gate; the FR-04 refinement is a precision improvement, not a gate workaround.

## Why it matters

Spec 220's born-green property (a produced tenant repo ships with a verified governance certificate and passes CI on birth) is undercut if the very first push shows a red check. This keeps produced repos green from birth while preserving admin-gated Pages enablement.

title: spike: hiqlite-in-Encore.ts NAPI feasibility (Shape A PoC + report)
body:
## What

Feasibility spike: can `hiqlite` be embedded **directly** into Encore.ts tenant
apps as an in-process native capability via napi-rs (cache / dlock / counters /
listen_notify), rather than a network sidecar? Two shapes were evaluated:

- **Shape A**: a standalone napi-rs addon linking hiqlite, imported by the app.
- **Shape B**: forking Encore's Rust runtime to add hiqlite as a first-class
  Encore primitive.

This is strategic / forward-looking. There is **no live gap** (rate-limiting
stays Postgres; there is no Redis in the stack). This branch is a **throwaway
spike for review and record**, not a feature intended to merge to `main` as-is.

## Verdict

**Neither shape as a near-term build.**

- **Reject Shape B outright.** No plugin seam exists; a new primitive is a
  4-surface fork (encore-runtime-core + encore-js-runtime + the `encore.dev` SDK
  + the Go CLI's static-analysis codegen) tracking a weekly-releasing upstream.
- **Hold Shape A in reserve.** Technically clean and **proven buildable** (see
  PoC below), but it is a delivery mechanism for a value case that does not exist
  yet for tenant apps: a shared cross-replica cache requires StatefulSet Raft
  clustering that fights Encore's autoscaled-Deployment model. Absent that, an
  in-process map or Postgres wins.

Full analysis (Q1 through Q6, licensing, costs) in
[`docs/analysis/hiqlite-napi-feasibility.md`](docs/analysis/hiqlite-napi-feasibility.md).

## PoC (executed, green)

`experiments/hiqlite-native-spike/` (throwaway): a napi-rs addon linking hiqlite
`=0.13.2` (single-node, cache-only, no SQLite-C) exposing `put`/`get`, called
from one Encore.ts endpoint.

- **Q2 (two tokio runtimes): CONFIRMED.** Under `encore run`, `put`/`get`
  round-trips through Encore into napi into hiqlite. hiqlite's tokio (in the
  addon's own dylib) coexists with Encore's Rust runtime in one process, no
  contention or nested-runtime panic.
- **Q4 (`encore build docker` bundles + loads the native addon): CONFIRMED.**
  A cross-built Linux `.node` bundled into the image and loaded at runtime; the
  same round-trip works in-container.

Real costs (all in native distribution, not runtime coexistence): cross-build the
addon per target yourself; ship a real npm package with per-platform
`optionalDependencies` (not a `file:` symlink); `bundle_source` over an
npm-workspace root bundles the whole repo (needs a `.dockerignore`); the
self-host gateway binds `:8080`. Details and reproduce steps in
[`experiments/hiqlite-native-spike/RESULTS.md`](experiments/hiqlite-native-spike/RESULTS.md).

## Not in this branch

Prebuilt `.node` binaries, napi-generated loaders, Rust `target/` output, and
`node_modules` are gitignored. `RESULTS.md` has the exact commands to regenerate
and re-run everything.

title: fix(005,ci): carry SPA build placeholder into born-with apps; tolerate npm-ls overrides in SBOM
body:
## What

Two born-with CI blockers surfaced by a fresh Single scaffold
(`stagecraft-ing/spec220-ac2-single-2`, OAP spec 220 AC-2). Both are fixed here so
the produced app's whole CI (`ci-gate`), not just the cert chain, runs green.

## Why

### 1. `encore check` fails: "unable to read static assets directory"

`apps/api/web/static.ts` serves the SPA via `api.static({ dir: "./build" })` (spec
005 FR-002). Only the committed placeholder `apps/api/web/build/index.html` is
tracked, so the app graph can build before a real SPA build exists. But the
repo-root `.gitignore` has a blanket `build/` rule. On a produced app's fresh
`git init && git add` (a born-with scaffold), that rule prunes the whole
`apps/api/web/build/` directory, and git cannot re-include a file whose parent
directory is pruned, so `apps/api/.gitignore`'s `!/web/build/index.html` negation
is powerless. The placeholder is dropped from commit #1 and `encore check` (and
`gen:client`) fail. The template repo itself is unaffected because the placeholder
is already tracked there (a fresh add never re-evaluates it).

**Fix:** add an explicit `!apps/api/web/build/` negation to the root `.gitignore`
so the deeper `apps/api/.gitignore` file-level rules apply (ignore `build/*`, keep
`index.html`). Spec 005 FR-003 is amended to require the root negation for
born-with apps.

### 2. SBOM generation fails: `npm-ls exited with errors (ELSPROBLEMS)`

`@cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm` shells out to `npm ls`, which exits non-zero because the
app's `overrides` force `glob@13` / `editorconfig@3` outside a transitive
dependent's declared range. Under node-24 (CI since the node-22 bump) that aborts
the SBOM step, which skips the spec 220 cert emit + verify. This was previously
dismissed as a node-24-only "false alarm"; it is the CI default now.

**Fix:** add `--ignore-npm-errors` to both cyclonedx invocations (generation +
parity re-check). The BOM is lockfile-derived (`--package-lock-only
--output-reproducible`), so tolerating the tree range-validity warnings changes
neither its content nor its reproducibility; both invocations carry the flag so
their output hashes still compare byte-identical.

## Verification

- `.gitignore` fix: reproduced the drop in a clean `git init && git add`
  (placeholder dropped with the current root gitignore; kept with the negation, and
  real `assets/` output stays ignored).
- SBOM fix: reproduced `npm-ls exited with errors` without the flag; with it, a
  valid 471-component CycloneDX BOM is produced.
- `spec-spine@0.10.0 index check`: fresh. `spec-spine couple`: clean (SBOM change
  waived below).

Spec-Drift-Waiver: .github/workflows/spec-spine.yml adds --ignore-npm-errors to the cyclonedx SBOM step. The SBOM step behavior is governed by OAP spec 203 and vended into template-encore as born-with CI; the overrides-forced glob@13/editorconfig@3 make npm-ls exit ELSPROBLEMS under node-24, and the BOM is lockfile-derived so reproducibility is unchanged. No template-encore spec design changes; there is no local owning spec to amend.

title: feat(000): seed born-with BRD placeholder so produced apps pass verify-provenance
body:
## What

Seed a claimless born-with BRD placeholder at
`requirements/business-requirements-document.md`, carried into every produced app
by the born-with generator.

## Why

A freshly scaffolded produced app ships no BRD. The born-with CI step "Claim
provenance verify" (OAP spec 209 FR-001, spec 121) runs `tenant-tail
verify-provenance --project . --fail-on-rejected`, a deliberate fail-closed gate:
a missing BRD (`brdNotFound=true`) exits 1 ("nothing was verified"). That failure
skips the downstream "Emit governance certificate" (OAP spec 220 FR-002) and
"verify-certificate" (spec 209 FR-001) steps, so **every produced app is born
red** and the OAP spec 220 AC-2 cert chain never runs green.

Observed on a real scaffold (`stagecraft-ing/spec220-ac2-single`):

```
provenance verification FAILED: no BRD found under the project; nothing was verified (--fail-on-rejected)
```

## How

Ship a placeholder BRD with a heading and prose but **no `### KIND-NNN` claim
headings**. With zero authored claims the audit has nothing to reject, so
`verify-provenance --fail-on-rejected` exits 0 and the cert chain proceeds. This
is the same shape as tenant-tail's own `cert-run` fixture BRD, so it keeps the
fail-closed contract intact (no ASSUMPTION gate-gaming). App authors replace the
placeholder with real requirements; each `### KIND-NNN` heading then becomes a
claim the gate re-checks.

`spec 000-bootstrap` establishes and describes the placeholder (Territory table +
the born-with BRD note in the CI behavior section).

## Verification

- `tenant-tail@0.3.0 verify-provenance --project <dir> --fail-on-rejected` against
  the exact shipped content: **exit 0** (`total=0 rejected=0 brdNotFound=false
  unparsedInlineCount=0`).
- `spec-spine@0.10.0 index check`: **fresh** (`.derived` regenerated for
  000-bootstrap).
- Coupling satisfied: 000-bootstrap establishes the new path and its `spec.md`
  changed in this PR.

title: fix(ci): inherit secrets to spec-spine gate; fix parentless-commit routing
body:
## What

Fixes two born-with CI defects that a **produced app** hits on its very first commit. Both were invisible in this template's own CI (the template has no `.kernel-version`, so the cert-emit legs are no-ops), so they only surface once a real tenant is scaffolded.

### 1. `secrets: inherit` on the spec-spine gate (the real cert-emit blocker)

`ci.yml` dispatched the reusable `spec-spine.yml` workflow via `uses:` **without** `secrets: inherit`. A reusable workflow receives none of the caller's secrets unless they are inherited, so `secrets.OAP_SIGNING_KEY` was empty inside it and the terminal `tenant-emit build-certificate` step (spec 220 FR-002) took its "key unavailable, skip emission" branch **every run**, even though the platform provisions the secret at project creation (spec 220 FR-003). The certificate was never emitted, so spec 209's dormant verify step never activated.

Fix: `secrets: inherit` on the `spec-spine` job, matching the existing `ai-review` job. Inherited secrets are simply empty on fork PRs, which preserves the emit step's documented graceful skip.

### 2. Parentless-initial-commit route computation (exit 128)

The `changes` route job resolved the push base with `git rev-parse HEAD~1 2>/dev/null || git rev-parse HEAD`. On a **parentless initial commit** (a produced app's commit #1, where `github.event.before` is the zero SHA) `git rev-parse HEAD~1` cannot resolve and, without `--verify`, echoes the literal `HEAD~1` to stdout. The result is a two-line `base` that breaks the subsequent `git diff` with `fatal: ambiguous argument` (exit 128), failing the whole run.

Fix: `git rev-parse --verify --quiet HEAD~1` (silent, non-zero on failure) with a `git hash-object -t tree /dev/null` empty-tree fallback, so every path registers as changed and all routes compute.

## Spec

Spec 009 FR-01 (push / initial-commit routing) and FR-02 (`secrets: inherit` on the spec-spine gate) amended to document both behaviors. Codebase index regenerated for the spec.md change.

## Verification

Local gates green on the branch: `spec-spine compile` / `index check` (fresh) / `lint --fail-on-warn` (0/0/0) / `couple` (0 paths, no drift). End-to-end proof of the cert chain with both fixes applied to a produced app: a scaffolded tenant's born-with CI emitted a signed certificate and `tenant-tail verify-certificate` accepted it green (`governance certificate VERIFIED`, corpus + SBOM bindings VERIFIED). This is the template-source half of that fix (the produced-app scaffold source-fixes ride in companion PRs on `factory-encore` and the platform scaffold).

## Context

Unblocks OAP spec 220 AC-2 (produced-app CI emits a cert the spec 209 verify accepts green).

This release focuses on Node HTTP adapter fixes, safer AxiosError serialisation, runtime/type correctness fixes, documentation updates, and dependency maintenance.

  • AxiosError Serialisation: Made AxiosError#cause non-enumerable to prevent circular JSON serialisation failures when errors include nested causes. (#10913)

  • Runtime and Type Correctness: Fixed several runtime crashes, type definition mismatches, and incorrect error handling paths. (#10959, #11021)

  • Dependencies: Bumped vite, rollup, form-data, js-yaml, and multer across the root project, docs, smoke tests, and module test workspaces. (#11011, #11012, #11013, #11014, #11015, #11016, #11017, #11026)

title: refactor(specs): renumber corpus to serial 000-016 (close gaps)
body:
## Why

The spec corpus skipped numbers. Specs `007-010` and `020` were migrated to the sibling `factory-encore` repo, leaving holes plus a `019 -> 021` jump. Serial numbering is non-negotiable for `000/001/002…`, so this closes every gap.

## What

Renumber by **compaction**, preserving chronological/topic order, so the corpus is contiguous `000-016`. `000-006` are unchanged; ten specs shift down:

| old | new | | old | new |
|-----|-----|---|-----|-----|
| 011-encore-ci-cd | **007** | | 016-enterprise-actions-governance | **012** |
| 012-container-host-deploy | **008** | | 017-ai-pr-review | **013** |
| 013-repo-ci-orchestrator | **009** | | 018-claude-skills | **014** |
| 014-supply-chain-gates | **010** | | 019-claude-config-governance | **015** |
| 015-workflow-pins-lint | **011** | | 021-docs-website | **016** |

Every reference updated atomically:
- 10 directory renames (git rename-detected) + `id:` frontmatter + H1 headers
- cross-spec `depends_on` / `target_specs` / `constrains` edges
- full-slug and short-form (`spec NN`, `` `NN` ``, ranges, lists) body references
- `.github/` workflow `# Spec:` headers, CODEOWNERS, dependabot, PR template
- `docs/**`, the Docusaurus `website/**`, `.claude/**`, `spec-spine.toml`
- `.derived/**` registry + index regenerated from source

## Gate

```
compiled 17 spec(s), 0 warnings
lint: 0 error(s), 0 warning(s)
index is fresh
couple --base origin/main: 32 path(s) checked, no drift
workflow-pins: PASS
```

No `Spec-Drift-Waiver` required: every changed owned path has its owning spec changed in the same diff (`000-bootstrap` itself was edited, covering CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md).

## Note on factory-encore

Per maintainer guidance, references that point at migrated specs assume `factory-encore` is being compacted in parallel with the same strategy. This repo carries no factory-encore spec-number references to remap (only the repo name and unrelated OAP spec numbers, which are untouched).

body:
## Summary

Adds a complete Docusaurus v3 documentation website under `website/` with 24 authored pages covering the full architecture, security model, governance, and developer workflow, plus the GitHub Pages publish workflow. The site and its workflow are governed by new spec `021-docs-website`.

## What's Included

- **Docusaurus 3.10.1** (classic preset, TypeScript) with `@docusaurus/theme-mermaid` for architecture diagrams
- **24 documentation pages** across 7 sidebar categories:
  - Getting Started (overview, prerequisites, quick-start, project structure)
  - Concepts (architecture, backend services, auth model, BFF gateway, security invariants, frontend, data/persistence)
  - Guides (dev workflow, auth setup, deployment, testing, scaffolding features, troubleshooting)
  - Reference (API endpoints, configuration, CLI/scripts, Encore.ts reference, custom Dockerfile, placeholders)
  - Governance (spec-spine overview, spec corpus)
  - Use with Claude Code (agentic surface, agents & skills, config governance)
  - Project (contributing, security)
- **Landing page** with hero section, install block, and four feature cards
- **`onBrokenLinks: throw`** ensures link integrity at build time
- **`static/.nojekyll`** for GitHub Pages underscore-prefixed asset support

## GitHub Pages Workflow

`.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml` builds the site (`npm ci` + `npm run build` in `website/`) and publishes it to GitHub Pages. All five `actions/*` refs are SHA-pinned per spec 015, and the workflow uses only allow-listed first-party publishers per spec 016. It is inert until a repo admin enables Pages.

## Governance

New spec `021-docs-website` (kind: feature, domain: ci-cd) establishes `website/` and `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml`, so both the site and its publish workflow are spec-owned and traceable. The spec registry and codebase index are recompiled in this branch; the coupling gate passes with no waiver.

## Build Verification

```
npm run build   # SUCCESS: Generated static files in "build".
```

## Setup Requirement

After merging, enable GitHub Pages in repository Settings → Pages → Source: **GitHub Actions**.

title: ci(017): AI PR review API-failure resilience (pass with visible notice)
body:
## What

Ports the OAP **spec 177** AI-review resilience posture into template-encore's `ai-pr-review.yml`. A Claude API outage must not block merges, but a pass must never be silent.

The **Run AI Review** step now classifies a `claude` failure instead of failing blindly:

| Failure class | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` unset | **hard fail** (config bug; unchanged) |
| auth / permission error (`authentication_error`, 401/403, invalid/expired/revoked token) | **hard fail**: a broken token must be fixed, not masked (preserves the anti-silent-green guard) |
| anything else (`overloaded_error`, `rate_limit`, 5xx, timeout, network, unclassified) | **PASS** with a loud `::warning::` + a PR notice; `ci-gate` rides through the incident |

## Changes
- `Run AI Review` gets `id: aireview`; the bare `claude -p` call is wrapped in classify-on-failure logic that writes `review_status` (`ok` / `api_failure`) to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.
- `Post review comment` is gated on `review_status == 'ok'` so a partial/empty review is never posted.
- New `Post API-failure notice` step posts a **visible** PR comment when the review was skipped due to an API outage. The pass is never silent.

## Why now
The 2026-06-23 Anthropic elevated-error-rate incident made `claude -p` exit non-zero, turning `ci-gate` red and blocking merges on any PR scanned during the window. A third-party API outage must not gate merges.

## Notes
- No new `uses:` refs; existing SHA pins untouched.
- The merge queue (`merge_group`) is unchanged and remains inert until a repo admin enables it.
